title: Reviewer, Not Data-Entry Clerk
description: The distinction between checking that a field is filled and checking that it's actually correct — the whole reason this track exists as a review role, not an entry-level coding job.

title: What This Role Actually Is
description: Describe the reviewer role in an AI-assisted coding pipeline and how it differs from manual coding — why the review queue is a filter concentrating the pipeline's own hardest cases, not a random sample, and what a reviewer is actually accountable for when they approve a claim.

title: Reading Clinical Documentation
description: Read a clinical note well enough to tell what actually happened to the patient — the SOAP structure, certainty language that changes codability, dual-meaning abbreviations, copy-forward tells, and what an absence in the note can and can't confirm.

title: The Coding Systems
description: Navigate ICD-10-CM, CPT/procedure coding, and the clinical terminologies (SNOMED CT, LOINC, RxNorm) well enough to check somebody else's — or an AI's — code selection, including catching version drift and skipping pattern-matching for a proper lookup.

title: How the AI Assigns a Code
description: Explain how an automated coding pipeline reaches a code — the extract/map/score/route stages, what a confidence score does and doesn't mean, why it favors common codes over correct ones, how negation trips it up, and where a correction actually lands — so you can predict where it will fail.

title: The Reviewer's Own Failure Mode
description: Recognise and counter the drift toward approving whatever the system suggests — why automation bias is specifically dangerous on a self-selected review queue, what a genuine check looks like versus a fast one, how volume pressure reinforces the drift, and how to build a personal check routine and self-audit that catch it before an external audit does.
